label: Series of causes
resolution: The no-regress premise STMT-NO-INFINITE-PER-SE-MOVER-SERIES is stated only for per se links (`MovesAsMoved`); nothing on the root path says that a per accidens series must end. ST I q.46 a.2 ad 7 grants that a per accidens series (an infinite past of fathers or hammers) is not impossible (STMT-INFINITE-REGRESS-IMPOSSIBLE-ONLY-IN-PER-SE-SERIES), so an eternal world does not touch the prima via. The series is per se because of STMT-SECOND-MOVERS-MOVE-ONLY-AS-MOVED, and it is read at one time (simul). The secunda via has its own per se link between efficient causes, `CausesAsCaused` (DEF-PER-SE-EFFICIENT-CAUSE-LINK), with its own no-regress premise STMT-NO-INFINITE-PER-SE-EFFICIENT-CAUSE-SERIES. It is not identified with `MovesAsMoved`: the only passage from one to the other is the explicit premise STMT-PER-SE-MOVER-LINK-IS-PER-SE-CAUSE-LINK (q.46 a.2 ad 7, the stone, stick and hand), from which AQUINAS-ST-I-Q46-A2-AD7-MOVER-REGRESS-FROM-CAUSE-REGRESS derives the mover regress premise. The here-and-now/removal descriptions of both primitive link relations are intended OPEN readings, not consequences of their types. The typed analyst sibling STMT-PER-SE-HISTORICAL-SERIES-DISTINCTION preserves the old source transcription: it proves exclusion under an explicit historical-to-essential edge dictionary and formal compatibility without that dictionary, with nonempty essential dependence on the same historical members. This does not establish a possible infinite past, all per-accidens series, or the well-foundedness premise. See docs/causal-regress-and-grim-reapers.md. Existential sense (#1926, 2026-11-24): SERIES_OF_CAUSES_4 (definition 57348ddc, DependenceOrderSenses.CausesBeingAsCaused) is the per se link of a present series of efficient causes of being: here and now c efficiently causes x's being, per se as caused (the PER_SE_5 primitive AsCaused). It is an analyst sense, not attributed to the secunda via, whose read text and ad 7 examples (movers; generation) do not restrict the series to causes of being. It is not identified with SERIES_OF_CAUSES_3 (CausesAsCaused, labelled CAUSES_AS_CAUSED_3 in DEF 4a101a4c and in the #1942 records): the only passage from SERIES_OF_CAUSES_4 to SERIES_OF_CAUSES_3 is the explicit open bridge 'every SERIES_OF_CAUSES_4 link is a SERIES_OF_CAUSES_3 link', listed as a sense bridge where an argument uses both senses; no passage from SERIES_OF_CAUSES_3 to SERIES_OF_CAUSES_4 is asserted, and the hand-and-stick case (a SERIES_OF_CAUSES_3 link through c2880fe0 that causes no being) falsifies one.
